How accents work in Italian
The most common accents are grave (`) and acute (´), usually found on vowels at the end of a word.
They show where the stress falls and sometimes change the vowel quality.
Accents also distinguish meanings in words that look the same otherwise.
Common examples: papà (dad), però (but), città (city).
